g.text: The duality — and the aggregate it depends on
sum changelog differences to [5, 3, 2, 6, 8] — exact · max changelog is consistent with ≥ 36 histories
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · table a:24 b:21 · total 45
FOLDING KEY "a"'S EVENTS INTO ONE VALUE
each row is one fold step; the last one is the table's value
after id 0 (+5)
balance 0 → 5
after id 1 (+3)
balance 5 → 8
after id 3 (+2)
balance 8 → 10
after id 4 (+6)
balance 10 → 16
after id 8 (+8)
balance 16 → 24
The table's value for key "a" is 24, and it is nothing but the last line of this fold.
Which means the table is not a separate thing that must be kept in sync — it is a FUNCTION of the stream, and can always be recomputed.
Step 1/4 — stream → table by aggregation
Stream to table is a fold, and the whole right-hand column is the proof: 24 is the last line of it. That matters architecturally — a table that is
a function of the stream cannot drift from it, whereas two independently-written stores can and will.
The duality — and the aggregate it depends on
sum changelog differences to [5, 3, 2, 6, 8] — exact · max changelog is consistent with ≥ 36 histories
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · table a:24 b:21 · total 45
CDC — EVERY CHANGE TO THE TABLE, AS A RECORD
this is what change-data-capture emits when the table is written
changelog record 1
key "a": old 0 → new 5
changelog record 2
key "a": old 5 → new 8
changelog record 3
key "a": old 8 → new 10
changelog record 4
key "a": old 10 → new 16
changelog record 5
key "a": old 16 → new 24
Each record carries BOTH values. That is what makes the changelog a stream you can fold back into a table, rather than a log of final states.
Carrying only the new value is the common mistake, and the next step prices it.
Step 2/4 — table → stream by change capture
Table to stream is change capture: watch the table and emit a record per write. This is how a database becomes a stream. The detail that makes it
work is in each row — the record carries the **old** value as well as the new, which is what the next step shows to be load-bearing rather than
decorative.
The duality — and the aggregate it depends on
sum changelog differences to [5, 3, 2, 6, 8] — exact · max changelog is consistent with ≥ 36 histories
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · table a:24 b:21 · total 45
THE LAST UPDATE, INTO TWO KINDS OF CONSUMER
the same update, with and without the old value
the update
record carries only the NEW value, consumer SUMS
record carries OLD and NEW, consumer sums
so a changelog is not a list of values
it is a list of (retraction, assertion) pairs
This is ch02's accumulation question arriving from the other direction: a changelog record IS an accumulating pane, and the old value IS the
retraction.
A consumer that can only add is correct only if the producer supplies the undo. Nothing in the data reveals a mismatch.
Step 3/4 — and a new-value-only changelog breaks a summing consumer
The same mechanism as ch02's retraction, reached from the table side. A record saying "the balance is now 24" sums to 40 in a consumer that adds;
a record saying "it was 16, it is now 24" sums to 24. The old value is not metadata — it is what makes the changelog invertible.
The duality — and the aggregate it depends on
sum changelog differences to [5, 3, 2, 6, 8] — exact · max changelog is consistent with ≥ 36 histories
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · table a:24 b:21 · total 45
THE ROUND TRIP, FOR A SUM AND FOR A MAX
the same duality, applied to two aggregates
key "a"'s actual event values
SUM changelog (new values)
[5, 8, 10, 16, 24] → differences [5, 3, 2, 6, 8] — recovered exactly
MAX changelog (new values)
[5, 5, 5, 6, 8] → differences [5, 0, 0, 1, 2] — NOT the events
event sequences consistent with that max log
at least 36 — the round trip is lossy
A sum is invertible: differencing the changelog recovers every event. A max is not — the 2 zero-deltas each hide any value up to the running max.
So "aggregating the changelog reproduces the table, and capturing the table reproduces the changelog" is true of the TABLE, and not of the
original events.
Step 4/4 — but "the directions are inverses" depends on the AGGREGATE
This is the refinement the duality usually gets stated without. Differencing the sum changelog gives back [5, 3, 2, 6, 8] — exactly the events.
Differencing the max changelog gives [5, 0, 0, 1, 2], and at least 36 different event sequences produce that same log. The round trip recovers the
*table* either way; it recovers the *events* only for an invertible aggregate.
